extracted.intended_audience: Executive departments and agencies, OIRA (Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs), OMB, regulatory policymakers, and stakeholders participating in federal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Executive Order 14094 provides standards and procedural guidance for federal regulatory review, notice-and-comment processes, OIRA meetings, and regulatory analysis, with emphasis on inclusive public participation, transparency, equity, and modernization of tools and guidance (including A-4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant regulatory action (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Significant regulatory action" means any regulatory action that is likely to result in a rule that may: (1) have an annual effect on the economy of $200 million or more (adjusted every 3 years by the Administrator of OIRA for changes in gross domestic product); or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector of the economy, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State, local, territorial, or tribal governments or communities; (2) create a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with an action taken or planned by another agency; (3) materially alter the budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights and obligations of recipients thereof; or (4) raise legal or policy issues for which centralized review would meaningfully further the President’s priorities or the principles set forth in this Executive order, as specifically authorized in a timely manner by the Administrator of OIRA in each case."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes explicit $200 million annual-effects threshold (adjusted every 3 years by OIRA for GDP changes). Retains and amends the definition in EO 12866 §3(f); these subparts are the criteria agencies and OIRA should use to determine when centralized review is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusive public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law, regulatory actions should be informed by input from interested or affected communities; State, local, territorial, and Tribal officials and agencies; interested or affected private-sector parties and other regulated entities; those with expertise in relevant disciplines; and the public as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opportunities for public participation shall be designed to promote equitable and meaningful participation by a range of interested or affected parties, including underserved communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition process clarification, responsiveness, and logging
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall, to the extent practicable and consistent with applicable law: (i) clarify opportunities for interested persons to petition for issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule under 5 U.S.C. 553(e); (ii) endeavor to respond to such petitions efficiently, in light of agency judgments of available resources and priorities; and (iii) maintain, subject to available resources, a log of such petitions received, and share with the Administrator of OIRA, upon request, information on the status of recently resolved and pending petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This imposes expectations of transparency and timeliness in petition handling and a record-keeping practice to support OIRA oversight and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive stakeholder engagement and accessibility best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: To inform development of regulatory agendas and plans, agencies shall endeavor, as practicable and appropriate, to proactively engage interested or affected parties (including underserved communities), consumers, workers and labor organizations, program beneficiaries, businesses and regulated entities, experts, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such efforts shall incorporate, to the extent consistent with law, best practices for information accessibility and engagement, including community-based outreach; outreach to organizations that work with affected parties; use of agency field offices; use of alternative platforms and media for engaging the public; and expansion of public capacity for engaging in the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize notice-and-comment to address mass and machine-generated comments
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator of OIRA, in consultation with relevant agencies, shall consider guidance or tools to modernize the notice-and-comment process, including through technological changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These reforms may include guidance or tools to address mass comments, computer-generated comments (such as those generated through artificial intelligence), and falsely attributed comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: OIRA meeting access, efficiency, and transparency reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce risk or appearance of disparate and undue influence in the OIRA review process, the Administrator of OIRA shall, to the extent practicable and consistent with law: (i) provide information to facilitate initiation of meeting requests regarding regulatory actions under OIRA review from potential participants not employed by the executive branch who have not historically requested such meetings; and (ii) implement reforms to improve procedures and policies with respect to OIRA’s consideration of meeting requests initiated by non-executive-branch persons regarding the substance of regulatory actions under OIRA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms may include: (A) efforts to ensure access for meeting requesters who have not historically requested such meetings; (B) discouraging meeting requests duplicative of earlier meetings with OIRA by the same requesters about the same action; (C) consolidation of meetings by requester, subject matter, or other consistently applied factors to improve efficiency; and (D) disclosure of data in an open, machine-readable, and accessible format including dates and names of individuals involved in all substantive meetings and the subject matter discussed, as required by EO 12866 §6(b)(4)(C)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory analysis should recognize distributive impacts and equity
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory analysis should facilitate agency efforts to develop regulations that serve the public interest, advance statutory objectives, and be consistent with EO 12866, EO 13563, and the Presidential Memorandum of January 20, 2021. Regulatory analysis, as practicable and appropriate, shall recognize distributive impacts and equity, to the extent permitted by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes equity and distributive-impact consideration as part of the analytic standards for regulatory development; it applies 'as practicable and appropriate' and 'to the extent permitted by law.'

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Circular A-4 revision and implementation timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 1 year of the date of this order, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, through the Administrator of OIRA and in consultation with the Chair of the Council of Economic Advisers and representatives of relevant agencies, shall issue revisions to OMB’s Circular A–4 (Regulatory Analysis) to implement the policy recognizing distributive impacts and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a binding timeline and process instruction to revise the principal federal guidance on regulatory analysis (Circular A-4) to reflect the policy in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and implementation constraints (legal and resource boundaries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect (i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or (ii) the functions of the Director of OMB relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals. This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also explicitly states the order is not intended to create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States or its officers, employees, agents, or any other person.
